title: Step 3: The Report
story: The librarian wants a printed list, oldest book first. Sort a copy so the shelf order does not change.
goal: Write Report() so it returns the numbered list, oldest first, one book per line.

tests.label: Two books, sorted by year
tests.expr: func() string { l := &Library{}; l.Add(Book{"Go", "Gopher", 2009}); l.Add(Book{"Malleshwari", "Rachakonda", 1950}); return l.Report() }()
tests.expect:
1. Malleshwari by Rachakonda (1950)
2. Go by Gopher (2009)

tests.label: The shelf order is not changed
tests.expr: func() string { l := &Library{}; l.Add(Book{"B", "y", 2000}); l.Add(Book{"A", "x", 1990}); l.Report(); return l.books[0].Title }()

tests.label: An empty library gives an empty report
main prints the report
tests.expect:
1. Malleshwari by Rachakonda (1950)
2. Go by Gopher (2009)

hints: Copy the slice first (make + copy), sort the copy with sort.Slice, then build the lines.
Use fmt.Sprintf("%d. %s", i+1, b) and strings.Join(lines, "\n").
socratic: What does sort.Slice need as its second argument?
Why does %s work on a Book?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Step 3: The Report”?
